items.label: Statements do not fetch listed fields
items.description: Reports db.query, db.get, db.add, db.edit, db.patch and db.add_or_edit statements whose output list fetches a listed or sensitive field of their table. Judges what each statement fetches into the object's stack, not the final response, so a field fetched but never returned is still reported. Sensitive means marked sensitive in the schema or password-typed; a password field is not reported when the record is used only through its other fields, a null check, or security.check_password, and returning or copying the whole record is reported. An absent or default output fetches every field, and an object or list field without narrowed children fetches every field inside it. Every nesting depth of the stack is inspected, and a dotted entry reaches inside a paged result (items.email). A field is only forbidden on a table that has it, and an output entry is attributed only through the statement's own declarations: a field of its own table, its own or a declared join alias as a prefix (user.email), or a literal eval alias; table.field restricts a name to that table. An entry whose provenance cannot be resolved (a runtime value, a computed eval, an undeclared prefix) is not reported, count, exists and aggregate queries fetch no record, and db.direct_query is not checked. Addons attached to the object's statements, and to statements in functions it calls, are always inspected against the addon's own table, narrowed by the attaching statement's selection. A function the object calls is followed, whatever the rule's scope, and what it fetches is reported on the caller; fixing the function clears every caller, and exempting a function with except_tags also exempts what callers reach through it. Middleware and tool mappings are not followed: each is judged as its own object. Exemption is per object: an exempted object is exempt for every listed field.

items.label: Reads and writes constrain a required field
items.description: Requires reads and writes of the selected tables to constrain field, against compare_to when set. Scope picks the objects inspected; table_selector picks which of their reads and writes are judged, empty meaning every table that has field. A db.query, db.get, db.bulk.delete or db.increment is judged by its where: a predicate counts only with =, in, contains or overlaps, on the statement's own table (a bare field or its own alias, not a joined one), and it must hold on every OR branch. An optional predicate (==?, in? …) is skipped at run time when its value is empty, so it never satisfies this rule. A selected table read as the primary table covers its joins; a selected table joined into an unselected one needs its own predicate, in the where or in its join condition. db.edit, db.patch, db.del and db.add_or_edit pass when they pick their row by field against compare_to, or by id = $o.id where $o is an earlier constrained read of the same table, or a foreach item over one, assigned nowhere else. The trace does not cross function calls, so a helper function writing by a passed-in id is reported (move the constrained read into it, or exempt it), and so is a write by $input.id after a precondition on the owner (write by $o.id instead). db.truncate on a selected table is always reported. Not checked: db.has (existence only), db.add (pin the owner with db.write_from_input_forbidden), db.bulk.patch, db.bulk.update and db.direct_query. To check only order's reads and writes, use table_selector: { names: ["order"] }; scope tables only picks which objects are inspected.

items.label: Writes don't take protected fields from input
items.description: Reports record writes taking their whole data, or a protected field, from input. Input is traced through variables, loops and data transforms. A write whose data is taken whole from input ($input or any $input.x) is mass assignment: whitelist the keys with pick, or build the object field by field. A pick as the last filter, with a literal key list, assigns exactly the picked keys; unset, unpick and set do not narrow the data. A record held in a variable assigned once (var, never changed after) is judged as the value assigned, and a function writing an argument whole is judged on what each caller passes, so a pick or an object literal there narrows it. Results of database, API and function calls are not treated as input. Input means request input for endpoints and middleware, arguments for AI tools and toolset triggers, and client messages for realtime triggers and message handlers; database-trigger rows and task runs are not input. Functions are judged through their callers: a write in a function is reported on the object passing it input, whatever the rule's scope, and exempting a function with except_tags exempts what callers reach through it. Agents calling functions as tools, and api.request into the workspace, are not followed.

items.label: Definitions avoid recognizable credential literals
items.description: Reports credential-shaped literals and literal keys in the selected locations. Findings name locations and pattern ids, never values. The definition location scans everything authored in each object (stack, inputs and defaults, response, settings, tests, descriptions), disabled content included since it is still stored and exported; env and agent settings are separate locations. Documentation examples (AWS keys ending EXAMPLE, the jwt.io sample token) are skipped. aws and twilio match identifiers rather than secrets, and some Google browser keys are public by design, though a backend literal still belongs in env. literal_keys reports literal keys and IVs passed to security.encrypt/decrypt, jws/jwe encode/decode and hmac_* filters, and literal bearer tokens passed to ai.external.mcp statements; public keys (PEM PUBLIC KEY/CERTIFICATE, JWKs without private members) are allowed. Each finding names the SHA-256 fingerprint of every value it reports, and a value whose fingerprint allowed_secrets lists is skipped.

patterns.description: Built-in patterns to match; empty means all, including ones added later. Custom regex is not supported.

locations.description: Where to scan: definition, env or agent_settings. Select at least one; env holds the workspace environment values. env is not scanned by default, because an environment variable is where a secret belongs.

allowed_secrets.description: Fingerprints ("sha256:" + 64 lowercase hex) of reviewed values to skip; never the values. Each is the SHA-256 of a value you allow wherever this rule looks, such as a public browser key or a test fixture; a raw value is refused. A literal is skipped when its whole text, or the text a pattern matched in it, is listed; each finding names the fingerprints of what it reports. Studio hashes a pasted value in the browser. An entry that allows nothing this rule reports is a rule warning.

items.label: Endpoint, tool and message inputs declare types, filters and bounds
items.description: Checks what endpoints, AI tools and message handlers declare as inputs. Enable at least one condition. Each condition can be its own rule; combine them only when they share severity and scope. Tools are included because a model chooses their arguments; functions are judged through their callers and are not inspected. path_params_forbidden applies to endpoints only. Nested object inputs are checked by dotted path (address.zip), a list of objects by element path (items.zip); json inputs have no declared shape. Without input_names, filter rules apply to every text input and unused_forbidden to every top-level input; input_names narrows them to exactly the named inputs, of any type. Filters are checked as declared on the input's type: min on an int bounds the value, on text its length. For paging, per_page is traced through variables, data transforms and called functions to each input reaching it; only a literal max filter on that input counts, bounding the value in code is not recognised, and the page (offset) input is not bounded by this condition. Middleware reads raw request params (as $input.vars.<name>) before the declared inputs are parsed, so a declaration does not validate what middleware reads, and an input read only by middleware is reported as unused. Called functions and the middleware resolution chain are read whatever the rule's scope.

items.label: Objects avoid forbidden settings
items.description: Reports objects whose settings match all configured predicates. Name settings from the kind's list. Raw storage paths are accepted, but a path found on no object makes the rule inert, with a warning. A listed setting compares its effective value: the stored value, else its default. present and absent test whether it is stored explicitly, and a raw path is always read as stored. Numeric predicates match only a numeric value, including a numeric string; in does not match a missing setting and not_in does, like not_equals. To bound a value use gt, e.g. cache.ttl gt 3600 reports a TTL above an hour; requiring a setting to exist needs a second rule with absent: true. A setting holding a secret (a key, token, password or credential) cannot be matched.

items.label: Objects call a required function or statement
items.description: Requires a matching statement, anywhere, where it always runs, or first. Called functions are followed; endpoints, AI tools, tasks and message handlers are inspected. A match is a listed statement that, when functions is set, calls one of them; any listed alternative satisfies the rule. Called functions are read whatever the rule's scope and except_tags: a match in one counts when the call is synchronous, no function on the way caches its result (a cached function skips its checks on cache hits), and, for unconditional, every call site on the way always runs too. A match in an attached pre-middleware counts when its exception policy is critical or rethrow, since a silent middleware swallows its failure; the middleware resolution chain is read whatever the rule's scope. In a called function or middleware, must_reference is met only by $auth and $env references. unconditional means at the top level of the stack or inside group, db.transaction, finally, or a try whose catch rethrows; not inside a conditional, switch, loop, catch or util.post_process. first means the object's own first statement, a comment skipped; a callee or middleware never counts as first. when selects objects by a statement in their own stack or in a function they call, and a read matches when.tables through the addons it attaches.

statements.description: Statements to require, any one of them. Set statements or functions; with both, the statement must call one of the functions. Exact XanoScript name (e.g. db.add or api.request) or registered stored name (e.g. mvp:dbo_add). A name that matches no statement is a rule warning. No regex or wildcards (only stack.statement_forbidden takes x.*).

functions.description: Custom functions to require a call to, any one of them. Exact names; a name not on the branch is a rule warning.

placement.description: any counts a match anywhere; unconditional one that always runs; first the first statement.

must_reference.description: Require every listed reference on the matching statement. Matches a reference or its child paths: $auth matches $auth.id, while $input.id does not match $input.id2. Quoted text is literal.

when.description: Only inspect objects with a statement matching every condition below; empty inspects every object in scope. Called functions are searched too, and objects without a match are not counted.

statement.description: Exact XanoScript statement name or stored alias.

tables.description: Exact names of tables the statement reads or writes, directly or through attached addons; any one matches.

fields.description: Exact assigned field names; any match qualifies. A dynamic whole-record assignment also qualifies.

hosts.description: Hostnames in a literal URL or literal URL prefix, matched case-insensitively; any one matches, and a leading dot matches a domain and its subdomains.

items.label: Outbound calls go only to approved vendors
items.description: Reports outbound destinations not on the approved lists. Empty allowlists report destinations as not yet reviewed. The http kind covers api.request, stream.from_request, the ai.external.mcp statements, api.microservice to a dotted host, and file statements given a literal http(s) URL; a dynamic file value is usually a file resource and is not reported. cloud and email check the provider, agent.llm an agent's model provider; cloud.job runs locally and is excluded. db.external reads the host of a literal connection string of db.external.*.direct_query. lambda scans literal api.lambda code: its literal URLs are checked, and network calls without one are reported as unverifiable. items.label: A statement comes before another
items.description: Requires every matching after statement, at any depth, to be preceded by a before that always runs ahead of it. Called functions and pre-middleware are followed. A before covers later statements of its own block, and reaches out of group, db.transaction, finally and a try whose catch rethrows; one inside a conditional branch, loop body, catch, a try that swallows failures or util.post_process covers only later statements in that same block. A guard in every branch of an if/else does not cover statements after the conditional (hoist it), and a guard written as conditional { throw } is not a before match (use precondition, or a guard function). An after in a function the object calls, not guarded inside that function, counts at the call site, async calls included; exempting the function with except_tags stops this. A synchronous call to a function holding an always-running before counts as a before at the call, unless a function on the way caches its result; an early return in a guard function before its check is not followed. An attached pre-middleware whose exception policy is critical or rethrow and that holds an always-running before covers the whole stack; a silent one does not. In a called function or middleware, must_reference is met only by $auth and $env references. A listed function counts only on a synchronous, uncached call; must_reference is checked on the call (its arguments), or through an $auth or $env reference inside the function. Objects with no after statement pass and are not counted. Called functions and the middleware chain are read whatever the rule's scope.

items.label: An expression follows reference and filter rules
items.description: Checks listed params for required or forbidden references, operators, literals and filters. References are traced through variables and called functions. A variable carries what is assigned to it (var and its mutators, foreach items, data transforms), and util.get_env, util.get_all_input, util.get_raw_input and util.get_vars carry everything they read; results of database, API and function calls carry nothing. must_not_reference fails when a listed reference may reach the param; must_reference is met by a reference written in the param, or by a variable every assignment of which carries it. Operators, literals and filters are read as written. A statement in a called function is judged through each caller: its $input means the arguments that caller passes, while $auth and $env keep their meaning; exempting a function with except_tags stops following it. $input is request data in endpoints, middleware, AI tools, message handlers and realtime or toolset triggers. In a database, workspace or error trigger, a task, and a function no in-scope object calls (judged on its own), $input is not request data: a $input entry in must_not_reference is not traced there, and one in must_reference is matched as written. So scope changes how a function is judged. An omitted parameter fails only a rule with must_reference or filters_required. Called functions are read whatever the rule's scope.

items.description: Requires a test that calls each endpoint requiring authentication anonymously and asserts the rejection. A tokenless endpoint unit test counts too. Tests are read, not run; every workflow test and the endpoints' unit tests are read whatever the rule's scope.

goals.goal: Endpoints require login
goals.summary: Every endpoint requires authentication, unless it or its API group is tagged public.
goals.limits: Checks the endpoint's saved authentication setting; what a logged-in caller is then allowed to do is not evaluated.

goals.goal: Endpoints don't return personal data
goals.summary: Endpoints never return the personal-data fields you list, or any field marked sensitive in its table's schema.
goals.limits: Judges what each database statement fetches, in the endpoint and the functions it calls, not the final response; a field fetched but never returned is still reported, and a response assembled by hand is not inspected. Only endpoints are judged: a function is reported on the endpoints that call it.

goals.goal: Users only reach their own records
goals.summary: Reads of owned tables filter on the owner field against the logged-in user, and new records take their owner from the login rather than the request.
goals.limits: Confirms the filter is written on each read, on every OR branch, and that writes pick a row the filter reached; an owner check done in a called function or after the read is not seen. Tasks and triggers have no logged-in user, so they are not judged; a public endpoint reading an owned table is reported, since it has no logged-in user to filter on.

goals.goal: No secrets are hardcoded
goals.summary: API keys, tokens, private keys, encryption keys and credentialed URLs are never written as literals in an object's definition or agent settings; they belong in environment variables.
goals.limits: Recognizes the built-in credential shapes and literal keys only; a secret in a format of your own is not matched. A value you reviewed is allowed by its fingerprint, never by the value itself.

goals.goal: Data only goes to approved vendors
goals.summary: Outbound requests, cloud and email providers and AI model providers are limited to the vendors you approve.
goals.limits: A destination built at run time is reported as unresolved unless it starts with a literal host or an approved environment variable, and what is sent to an approved vendor is not inspected.

goals.goal: Users can't make themselves admin
goals.summary: Record writes never take a privilege field such as role or is_admin from request input, nor a whole record from it.
goals.limits: Traces request input through variables, loops, data transforms and called functions; a value read back from the database or returned by an API or function call is not treated as input, and neither are agents calling functions as tools.

rules.title: Writes do not take privilege fields from the request

goals.goal: Public endpoints can't change data
goals.summary: An endpoint that requires no authentication never changes or deletes records.
goals.limits: Inspects the endpoint and the functions it calls, async calls included; middleware and agent tools are judged as their own objects, and a function tagged with one of the rule's except_tags is not followed.

rules.title: Public endpoints do not change or delete records

goals.goal: Admin endpoints check the caller's role
goals.summary: Every endpoint tagged admin calls your role-check function as its first statement, passing the logged-in user.
goals.limits: Confirms the call is written first, not what the function decides; an endpoint missing the admin tag is not examined.

rules.title: Admin endpoints call the role check first

goals.goal: No table truncation or raw SQL
goals.summary: No function stack truncates a table or runs a direct SQL query.
goals.limits: Matches the statements by name wherever they appear; SQL sent to an external database uses different statements, which you can add to the list.

rules.title: Truncation and raw SQL stay out

goals.goal: External requests verify TLS certificates
goals.summary: Every external request verifies the TLS certificate and host name of the server it talks to.
goals.limits: Reads each request's TLS flags, including variables assigned only literals and literal arguments to a function; a value computed at run time is reported as unverifiable. webflow.request is not checked: it runs without TLS verification whatever its flags say.

rules.title: Requests verify TLS certificates and hosts

goals.goal: Login tokens expire within an hour
goals.summary: Every authentication token expires within one hour of being created, and every signed token (JWS or JWE) within the lifetime you choose.
goals.limits: Reads the lifetime on each token statement, including variables assigned only literals and literal arguments to a function; an omitted one is judged at its runtime default (a day for an auth token, never expiring for a signed token), and a value computed at run time is reported as unverifiable. Choose the signed-token lifetime: session tokens usually allow minutes to an hour, emailed links (verification, reset) often a day; exempt objects that sign other payloads, such as webhook signatures.

rules.title: Tokens expire within one hour
Signed tokens expire

goals.goal: Endpoints are tested
goals.summary: Every endpoint is exercised by a workflow test or unit test that asserts something, and every protected endpoint has a test asserting that an anonymous call is rejected.
goals.limits: Inspects test definitions without running them, so a test that exists but fails still counts; an assertion must follow each call, but what it asserts is not checked. A workflow test cannot yet observe an anonymous call's rejection (api.call runs a protected endpoint anonymously), so that test fails until the platform enforces auth there; an endpoint unit test called without a token and expecting the rejection works today.

goals.goal: Sensitive tables are only reached by logged-in endpoints
goals.summary: Every endpoint that reaches a table carrying your sensitive-data tag, directly or through a function, requires authentication.
goals.limits: Depends on the tables being tagged; reaches tables through called functions and attached addons.

rules.title: Endpoints reaching sensitive tables require login

goals.goal: Sensitive fields are marked sensitive
goals.summary: The fields you list are marked sensitive wherever a table declares them.
goals.limits: Reads the table schemas only; a field holding personal data under a name you did not list is not found.

rules.title: Listed fields are marked sensitive

goals.goal: Tables holding confidential data are tagged
goals.summary: A table with a field you list, such as notes, carries the confidential tag.
goals.limits: Matches fields by exact name, nested fields included; a table holding the same data under another field name is not found.

goals.goal: Saved views hide sensitive fields
goals.summary: Every saved table view hides the fields marked sensitive in its table's schema, and password fields.
goals.limits: Checks saved views only: a share link made with the default view, or whose view was deleted, shares every field, and share links are outside the branch.

goals.goal: Logs don't contain request, user or secret data
goals.summary: Debug logs never reference request input, the logged-in user or environment variables.
goals.limits: Traces request input, the logged-in user and environment values through variables, data transforms and called functions; a value read back from the database or returned by an API or function call is not traced, and only debug.log is checked (add datadog.log with its message and attributes to cover it). Database-trigger rows and task runs are not request input, so logging them there is not reported.

rules.title: Logs name events, not input, auth or env

goals.goal: External calls handle their own failures
goals.summary: Every external request sits inside a try block, so a vendor failure reaches error handling.
goals.limits: Checks only the listed statements (add stream.from_request, ai.external.mcp.* and db.external.*.direct_query statements to cover every outbound call), on every call path; confirms each sits in a try block, not that every path through the catch handles the failure.

rules.title: Requests sit inside a try_catch

goals.goal: Middleware doesn't swallow errors
goals.summary: No middleware is set to swallow the exceptions it catches.
goals.limits: Reads each middleware's exception setting, a missing one counting as silent as it does at run time; what the middleware does with an error it surfaces is not evaluated.

rules.title: Middleware surfaces the exceptions it catches

goals.goal: External requests time out quickly
goals.summary: Every external request times out within 30 seconds, so one slow vendor cannot stall a workspace.
goals.limits: An omitted timeout is judged at its 10-second default. ai.external.mcp.* and db.external.* statements take no timeout and cannot be bounded; for stream.from_request the timeout bounds each read, not the whole stream, while for api.request it is the total time.

rules.title: External requests time out within 30 seconds

goals.goal: GET endpoints only read
goals.summary: A GET endpoint only reads data; every write sits behind a verb that says so.
goals.limits: Inspects the endpoint and the functions it calls, async calls included; middleware and agent tools are judged as their own objects, and a function tagged with one of the rule's except_tags is not followed. An audit function that writes (e.g. with db.add) makes every GET endpoint calling it fail: tag the audit function and add that tag to the rule's except_tags.

rules.title: GET endpoints only read

goals.goal: Endpoints check the caller before writing
goals.summary: Every authenticated endpoint that writes records checks the logged-in user with a precondition first.
goals.limits: Follows nested branches, called functions and pre-middleware; a check in only one branch covers only that branch, a check written as conditional { throw } is not a precondition, and an early return inside a guard function is not followed.

rules.title: A permission check precedes each write

goals.goal: Endpoint inputs are typed and bounded
goals.summary: Endpoint inputs declare suitable types and page-size limits, personal data stays out of URL paths, and every declared input is used.
goals.limits: Reads the declared inputs and the endpoint's stack; validation done inside a called function is not seen.

goals.goal: Protected endpoints run your auth middleware
goals.summary: Every endpoint that requires authentication runs the middleware you name.
goals.limits: Confirms the middleware is attached and active, not what it does.

rules.title: Protected endpoints attach the middleware

goals.goal: Users sign in through one auth table
goals.summary: The workspace has exactly one auth table, and every authenticated endpoint uses it.
goals.limits: Counts auth-enabled tables across the whole branch; several intentional auth tables mean this goal does not fit.

goals.goal: Only the audit function writes the audit log
goals.summary: The audit log table exists, and only the function you name writes to it.
goals.limits: Checks where each write is defined; a caller can still use the approved function to write whatever it passes in.

rules.title: The audit log table exists
Only the audit function writes it

goals.goal: Retained data has a cleanup task
goals.summary: Every table carrying your retained-data tag is referenced by a scheduled task that cleans it up.
goals.limits: Confirms an active task with a repeating schedule deletes from each table (db.del, db.bulk.delete, db.truncate, or a static db.direct_query), not that it deletes the right records; retention by anonymising (db.edit, db.patch or db.bulk.patch nulling fields) needs those statements added.

rules.title: Retained tables have a cleanup task

goals.goal: Trigger writes don't silently skip other triggers or re-fire themselves
goals.summary: A write made inside a trigger fires no other trigger, so a trigger that writes another table does not skip that table's own triggers, and one that writes its own table through an async function cannot re-fire itself.
goals.limits: Follows writes into called functions; writes made by an AI agent's tools are not followed, and a trigger's when-filter is not evaluated.

key.message: Policy key "%s" must be 1-64 chars of letters, digits, ".", "_" or "-", starting alphanumeric.

title.description: The policy's name, as lists, reports and runs show it.

statement.description: What the policy requires, in plain language. Put the guidance here too: why it exists, and what to do when an object cannot comply.

narrative.description: Longer notes on how the policy is implemented, in Markdown.

severity.description: How much a violation of this policy matters. It orders findings in reports and never blocks anything; enforcement does.

active.description: Only an active policy is evaluated; an inactive policy reports nothing.

enforcement.description: An advisory policy only reports. The findings of an active, mandatory policy are blocking.

tags.description: Labels, such as a framework and its criteria (soc2, cc6.1).

title.description: Optional. A rule without one is called by its check's label.

check.description: The id of the built-in check the rule runs.

params.description: The check's params: only those you set; the rest take their catalogue defaults.

policy.remediation: policy: "remediation" was removed; put the guidance in the policy statement.
policy.lifecycle: policy: "lifecycle" was replaced by "active"; write active = true or active = false.
policy.owner: policy: "owner" was removed; delete the line. Ownership will return as a reference to a workspace member.

rule.severity: rule[%d]: "severity" is set on the policy, not on a rule.
rule.remediation: rule[%d]: "remediation" was removed; put the guidance in the policy statement.

reserved_blocks.message: Policy block "%s" is reserved. Policies support rule blocks only.

rules_required.message: An active policy needs at least one rule; set active = false instead.
